title: Subcommand Router
prompt: Implement main(argv) (argv is a list like ['add', 'milk']) returning the exit code int: 'add' with text → prints 'added: <text>' and returns 0; 'list' → prints '2 tasks' and returns 0; unknown command or 'add' without text → prints the error to stderr and returns 2. (The grader captures stdout/stderr.)

tests.name: add prints and succeeds
tests.code:
import io, contextlib
buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
    code = main(['add', 'milk'])
assert code == 0 and buf.getvalue().strip() == 'added: milk'

tests.name: errors go to stderr with exit 2
tests.code:
import io, contextlib
out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
    code = main(['bogus'])
assert code == 2
assert err.getvalue().strip() != ''
assert out.getvalue() == ''
tests.hint: Error message to stderr; nothing on stdout; exit code 2.

tests.name: add without text is an error too
tests.code:
import io, contextlib
err = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
    code = main(['add'])
assert code == 2 and err.getvalue().strip() != ''
tests.hint: Missing required argument behaves like an unknown command.
